FY 2024 25 FY 2023 24 Gross billings Rs. 23356.37 Lakh Rs. 24218.26 Lakh Net revenue from operations Rs. 23196.28 Lakh Rs. 24103.11 Lakh Profit for the year Rs. -3,90,26,159 Rs. 753.38 Lakh The year under review saw steady execution across the Company's business units. Your Directors remain focused on disciplined bidding, timely certification of running-account bills and recovery of retention and statutory receivables. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION   OPERATING REVIEW The financial year under review was executed against an order book that the Board considers adequate for the near term. Revenue is recognised on the percentage-of-completion basis across the contract portfolio, and the movement in turnover between the comparative periods reflects the stage of execution reached on the larger packages rather than any change in the commercial terms on which work is taken. Margins remained within the range the Board regards as sustainable for this class of work. Input costs   principally cement, steel and bitumen   continued to move with the published indices, and where a contract carries a price-variation clause the recovery has been billed in the normal course. Where it does not, the exposure was absorbed within the tendered rates. Receivables continue to be dominated by government and public-sector clients, whose payment cycles are longer than those of private counterparties but whose credit risk the Board assesses as low. Retention money is released progressively on expiry of the defect liability periods, and no material amount is regarded as doubtful of recovery at the balance-sheet date. The Company met its statutory obligations in respect of goods and services tax, tax deducted at source and provident-fund contributions during the year, and holds current registrations for every jurisdiction in which it operates. STATE OF AFFAIRS & ORDER BOOK 17 contracts remained in execution as at year end with an aggregate awarded value of Rs. 56796.04 Lakh (including approved variations of Rs. 13823.06 Lakh across 75 variation orders). 7 credit notes aggregating Rs. 160.09 Lakh were absorbed in revenue. Retention money is released progressively on expiry of the defect liability periods, and no material amount is regarded as doubtful of recovery at the balance-sheet date. The Company met its statutory obligations in respect of goods and services tax, tax deducted at source and provident-fund contributions during the year, and holds current registrations for every jurisdiction in which it operates.
